data.title: A Carnival Attraction That Saved Premature Babies (2016)
data.author: pr337h4m
data.article_summary: Martin Couney was a renowned figure who ran infant incubator exhibits for over 30 years, most famously at Coney Island. His displays of premature babies in incubators drew large crowds, with an exhibit at the 1933-1934 Chicago World’s Fair being particularly successful. Couney, alongside pediatrician Dr. Julius Hess, cared for premature babies using advanced incubators, despite controversy over the ethics of displaying the infants. Couney claimed to have studied medicine in Europe, but evidence suggests he never officially qualified as a doctor. Despite this, his work saved thousands of babies and influenced American neonatal medicine, eventually gaining recognition as pioneering, though his lack of formal medical credentials remained a point of contention. His collaboration with Hess marked a significant step in gaining legitimacy in the medical field.

• matsemann没有直接讨论执照问题，而是通过讲述祖父的幽默故事，暗示一些看似荒唐或非传统的做法并不一定有害，尽管这些做法并非严格遵循常规。
• alsetmusic通过引用历史实例（"Infantorium"），指出在历史上一些看似奇怪的实践（如展示早产儿）也曾被社会接受，并强调这种现象在当时并非孤例，以此暗示判断实践方式的标准会随时间变化。
• delichon引用了《国王的演讲》中的例子，认为有些非传统或自学成才的从业者也能具备出色的能力，并对此表示鼓励。
• Aardwolf关注具体操作中的实际问题（如如何正确匹配婴儿和父母），质疑在实际操作中可能存在的管理问题，但没有直接评价实践方式的合法性或道德性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应拘泥于传统资格认证（如执照），还是更应看重实际结果和贡献。LinuxAmbulance明确反对过度关注过程，而其他评论者通过实例和个人故事间接支持这一观点。
• 历史实例（alsetmusic提供的"Infantorium"）为讨论提供了一个独特的视角，强调社会对专业实践的接受度会随时间变化。

• Aardwolf的评论提醒讨论中需要考虑的具体操作问题，如管理复杂性，这在实际应用中同样重要。

44770215.article_content:
Martin Couney holds up Beth Allen, a premature baby who was on view at the Coney Island attraction.
Beth Allen
Nurses in starched white uniforms and doctors in medical coats tended to babies in glass and steel incubators. The infants had been born many weeks premature and well below a healthy birth weight. Stores didn’t make clothes small enough to fit their tiny, skeletal frames so the nurses dressed them in dolls’ clothes and knitted bonnets.
A sign above the entrance read “Living Babies in Incubators” in letters so large they could be read from the other end of the Chicago World’s Fair grounds, which took place over 18 months in 1933 and 1934. The infant incubator exhibit was built at a cost of $75,000 (worth $1.4 million today) and was painted in a patriotic red, white and blue.
The men in charge were leading Chicago pediatrician Dr. Julius Hess and Martin Couney, who was known across America as “the incubator doctor.” Couney was a lugubrious man in his 60s, with thinning gray hair, a mustache and a stoop, something he jokingly attributed to a lifetime of bending over babies. Couney and Hess employed a team of six nurses and two wet nurses.
Martin Couney had run infant incubator exhibits, in which premature babies were displayed to the public, for more than three decades, most famously at Coney Island in New York City. He had long been regarded by desperate parents as a savior, one who offered medical help to babies written off as “weaklings” by mainstream medicine.
But for Hess, who was accustomed to carrying out his work in a more conventional hospital setting, this was a career first.
Miracle at Coney Island: How a Sideshow Doctor Saved Thousands of Babies and Transformed American Medicine (Kindle Single)
More about this product
The exhibit was a hit with the Chicago public who paid 25 cents and flocked by the hundreds of thousands to see the babies.
To celebrate the success of their facility, Couney organized a “Homecoming” celebration on July 25, 1934, for babies who had “graduated” from the incubators at the Chicago’s World’s Fair the previous summer. Of the 58 babies Couney and Hess had cared for in 1933, 41 returned with their mothers for the reunion. The event was broadcast live on local radio and across the fairgrounds.
On the radio program, Couney’s exhibit was portrayed by the announcer not as a frivolous sideshow spectacle, but as an invaluable medical facility:
The Incubator station for premature babies…is not primarily a place of exhibiting tiny infants. Instead, it is actually a lifesaving station, where prematurely born babies are brought from leading hospitals all over the city, for the care and attention that are afforded. The place is spick and span, with doctors and graduate nurses in constant attendance...
Because of the sideshow setting in which he operated, Couney’s career had always been controversial. Many in the medical professional viewed the “incubator doctor” with suspicion, others with outright hostility. The New York Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children had repeatedly accused Couney of exploiting the babies and endangering their lives by putting them on show.
None of the complaints was sustained, and by the 1930s, Couney was finally being taken seriously as a medical pioneer. Couney’s professional collaboration with Hess marked a key stage in his habilitation.
But while doing research for my radio documentary
Life Under Glass
, which is being broadcast on NPR stations around the country this August, and my book,
Miracle at Coney Island
, I made an incredible discovery about a man who has a claim to have changed the course of American neonatal medicine.
Couney never actually qualified as a medical doctor.
Throughout his career, Couney said he had studied medicine in Leipzig and Berlin. However, I could find no evidence of Couney (or Cohn/Cohen as he was known then) having studied medicine at a university in either city. To become a physician in Germany, one was required to write a thesis. The U.S. National Library of Medicine has copies of the German records: the librarians could not locate a thesis written by Couney.
Couney was deliberately evasive about his date and place of birth. I have discovered that he immigrated to the US in 1888 at 19 years old. But someone of that age would not be old enough to have studied at university in Leipzig and Berlin before going on to do graduate work in Paris at the knee of Pierre Budin, the father of European neonatal medicine, as Couney claimed to have done in numerous press interviews.
In the 1910 U.S. census, Couney listed his career as, “surgical instruments.” Though Couney claimed to be the inventor of an incubator, I have been unable to find any evidence that he registered an incubator patent in the U.S. More likely Couney was a technician. Yet by 1930 he was describing himself in the census as a “physician.”

data.title: Under the Hood of AFD.sys Part 1: Investigating Undocumented Interfaces
data.author: omegadev
data.article_summary:
本文是关于深入研究Windows 11中AFD.sys驱动程序系列的第一部分，重点在于通过I/O请求直接与AFD.sys交互，绕过Winsock接口创建TCP套接字。作者旨在创建一个绕过Winsock直接与AFD.sys通信的库，以便更深入理解Windows网络处理机制，并躲避反作弊和反恶意软件系统的监控。

文章详细描述了如何通过NtDeviceIoControlFile和手动构建的IRP与AFD驱动交互，以创建和配置套接字。作者参考了CVE-2024-38193的PoC代码，并通过尝试不同代码片段解决了创建套接字过程中的问题。

最终目标是构建一个C/C++核心库，并为Python和Rust添加易于使用的绑定接口，以便快速原型设计和脚本编写。后续文章将探讨通过该套接字进行实际数据交换和完整的TCP会话管理。

44776695.article_content:
Under the Hood of AFD.sys Part 1: Investigating Undocumented Interfaces
Contents
Under the Hood of AFD.sys Part 1: Investigating Undocumented Interfaces
Introduction
This is the first post in a series about my deep-dive into the
AFD.sys
driver on Windows 11. The idea is that both this write-up and the library that comes out of it will be a one-stop doc set - and a launchpad - for poking at other drivers that donât ship with an official spec.
On Windows, the go-to (and easiest) way to do network stuff is Winsock. It gives you a bunch of high-level calls for TCP/UDP and raw sockets over IPv4/IPv6. Under the hood Winsock rides on
mswsock.dll
, which is lower-level, but most apps never need to touch that because Winsock already covers 99 % of everyday networking needs.
In this first part weâre focusing purely on creating the socket itself. Step #1 is to open a TCP socket to any host on the LAN using nothing but I/O requests aimed at
\Device\Afd
. Instead of the usual Winsock calls (or anything in
mswsock.dll
) weâre going to slam everything through
NtDeviceIoControlFile
, hand-crafting the IRPs (I/O Request Packets) the AFD driver expects. Thatâll show us, in real life, how to build the call sequence, buffer layouts, and flags you need to spin up a TCP session.
The actual data exchange over that socket - the whole TCP conversation - will come in later posts.
Right now Iâve already collected all the data to pull off the TCP three-way handshake. Took me a few evenings to get there, so Iâm just jotting down what I did so far. Iâll keep adding the rest as I go - at least thatâs the plan!
What is AFD.sys?
The
AFD.sys
- or Ancillary Function Driver - is a small but absolutely basic Windows kernel driver. It sits in C:Windows32drivers and starts up with the system, because itâs the one that translates the Winsock calls of your applications (send, recv, connectâ¦) into lower-layer intelligible
IRP
(
I/O request packet
), which tcpip.sys and co. are already taking over. If it were missing, the browser, Spotify or remote desktop wouldnât see the network - all TCP/UDP traffic would simply stop.
Rationale
The first reason for talking directly to
AFD.sys
instead of going through Winsock is to dodge the hooks used by some protection systems - like anti-cheat or anti-malware (though the latter usually rely on NDIS filters in kernel mode). A lot of these protections work by intercepting and modifying calls to functions exported by
Ws2_32.lib
- usually by injecting their own DLLs or patching stuff directly in process memory. But if youâre not using Winsock, those hooks have nothing to latch onto, which makes their job way harder from a technical standpoint.
The second reason - and honestly the one that matters most to me - is the educational value. Working directly with
AFD.sys
gives you a deep look under the hood of how Windows handles networking. That kind of insight just isnât possible when you stick to high-level APIs.
The goal of this whole project is to build a library for talking directly to the
AFD.sys
driver on Windows 11, completely skipping the Winsock layer. The core will be written in C/C++ and will include all the low-level logic for building and sending IRPs. On top of that, Iâm planning to add clean, easy-to-use bindings for Python - great for quick prototyping or scripting - and also for Rust.
Dumb Copy&Paste
The very first thing we have to nail down is a socket the driver will actually accept, so we can start talking on the wire. While combing the internet I ran into a PoC for CVE-2024-38193
(killvxk)
. That was the first real bit of code that spat out a socket for me:

data.title: Some thoughts on journals, refereeing, and the P vs NP problem
data.author: luu
data.article_summary: Eric Allender撰文回应近期发表于《Springer Nature》旗下《Frontiers of Computer Science》期刊的一篇声称证明了P ≠ NP的不正确论文。Allender曾任《ACM Transactions on Computation Theory》主编，处理过许多类似声称解决P vs NP问题的投稿，通常由编委会成员寻找审稿人。然而，此次发表的论文《SAT Requires Exhaustive Search》在编辑过程中出现问题：几位复杂性理论专家表示未参与审稿，且论文中的主要定理被证明是错误的，尤其是与Ryan Williams二十多年前提出的算法结果相矛盾。论文附录引用了一些研究人员的赞誉，包括Gregory Chaitin，但他本人表示被误引。Allender和Williams建议撤稿但被拒，最终他们的评论将在期刊上发表，但删除了批评期刊和出版社的结尾段落。论文作者也提供了回应，但未获Allender认可。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一篇涉及P vs NP问题的论文及其回应的批评和讨论

不同观点：
• [pron]: 批评论文的回应质量差，指出论文中依赖的数学假设存在问题。作者认为，Turing的假设是跨越物理与数学的桥梁，而论文的假设是在数学内部的，可能根本就是错误的。将假设作为证明基础是不合适的，类似于通过假设某种情况存在来证明一个命题，而不是直接证明该命题。
• [zero_k]: 从实际工作经验出发，讨论了论文中关于约束满足问题（CSP）和计数问题的一些具体技术问题。他表示，在处理仅包含二元变量的CSP问题时，并没有发现比处理更长子句问题更高效的算法，质疑论文中声称的更高效算法的存在。
• [qsort]: 提到P vs NP问题吸引了大量非专业人士的关注，因为问题的表述相对简单，导致很多非专业人士尝试解决这一问题，产生了很多不严谨或错误的证明。
• [Xcelerate]: 建议使用形式化验证工具（如Lean）来自动验证涉及P vs NP问题的证明。认为通过形式化验证可以减少错误证明的发表，并提出期刊可以要求作者提供形式化验证版本的证明。
• [brohee]: 批评论文发表的期刊质量不高，并质疑编辑为何允许这种情况发生。认为对于重大结果应采取更严格的审查机制。

补充讨论：
• [shusaku]: 同意对期刊质量的批评，并指出学术欺诈的问题，认为如果结果真实，应该能在更好的期刊上发表。
• [brohee] 和 [shusaku] 都提到学术期刊的审查问题，认为应该对重大结果采取更严格的审查标准。
• [brohee] 还提到一个关于GPT-4生成论文质量的问题，质疑人工智能生成内容在学术领域的可靠性。

44808693.article_content:
A guest post by Eric Allender prompted by an
(incorrect) P ≠ NP proof
recently published
in Springer Nature's Frontiers of Computer Science.
For a time, I served as Editor-in-Chief of ACM Transactions on Computation Theory, and in this role I had to deal regularly with submissions that claimed to resolve the P vs NP problem. Finding referees for these papers was sometimes challenging, so I frequently ended up reviewing them myself.  Dealing with such submissions involves enough overhead that ToCT, J.ACM and ACM Transactions on Algorithms limit the frequency with which authors can submit work of this sort.  But for every submission, on any topic, the overall process was the same: Find someone on the Editorial Board who has sufficient expertise to find referees and make knowledgeable use of their recommendations.  If there was no such person on the Editorial Board, then it was always the case that the submission was out of scope for the journal.
These thoughts are brought to mind by a recent case, where it seems to me that the editorial process broke down.
Springer publishes several high-quality academic journals that deal with Theoretical Computer Science.  One Springer journal, Frontiers of Computer Science, recently published an article entitled
SAT Requires Exhaustive Search
, where one of the authors is a Deputy Editor-in-Chief of the journal.  The abstract of the article states that it proves a result that is stronger than P not equal to NP.  The Editorial Board of the journal has some members who are expert in computational complexity theory.  However, all the ones whom I know personally have asserted that they had no knowledge of this paper, and that they were not involved at all in handling the paper.
When Ryan Williams and I learned about the publication of this article, we drafted a
comment
, which we sent to the Editor-in-Chief.  We recommended that the paper be retracted, in which case there would be no need to publish our comment.  However, the Editor-in-Chief declined to retract the article, saying that he could find no evidence of misconduct, and thus we have been assured that an edited version of our comment will appear in the journal.
Our comment calls attention to some shortcomings in the proof of the main theorem (similar to shortcomings in several other failed attempts to separate P from NP).  But we were able to say more.  Often, when one is looking for bugs in a purported proof, one has to deal with the situation where the claimed theorem is probably true, and the only problem is that the proof is not convincing.  However, the main theorem in their paper (Theorem 3.2) states that a particular constraint satisfaction problem requires time more than \(d^{cn}\) for any constant \(c<1\) (where \(d\) is the domain size, and \(n\) is the number of variables).  In particular, their purported proof claims that this holds even when \(k=2\) (meaning that each constraint has at most 2 variables).  However, Ryan Williams
presented an algorithm
more than two decades ago that runs in time \(O(d^{(0.8)n})\) in this special case, contradicting the lower bound claimed in the article.
The article contains an appendix, with glowing testimonies from various researchers; the lead-in to the appendix also contains enthusiastic comments from Gregory Chaitin.  I contacted Gregory Chaitin, and he asserts that he did not read the paper, and that he was quoted out of context.
The edited version of the
comment
that Ryan Williams and I wrote, which will supposedly appear in Frontiers of Computer Science soon, differs from the version linked here (our original submission) primarily in one respect:  Our closing paragraph was removed.  Here is that paragraph:
Finally, it is our opinion that the publication of this article is a complete embarrassment to this journal and its publisher. We believe that, at the very least, the paper should be withdrawn, and Springer should conduct an investigation to understand how such a paper could have made it through the peer review process.
Update (Lance, 8/5/25):
The authors of the paper in question have asked me to link to
their reply to the Allender-Williams comment
. I do so with no endorsement.
Eric Allender asked me to note that their claim about Ryan’s algorithm requiring exponential space is misleading; the amount of space is not more than the runtime of the algorithm, which is less than the lower bound that they claim. (Their theorem does not state that \(d^{cn}\) time is required under the additional assumption that the algorithm use only \(n^{O(1)}\) space.)

data.title: Rethinking DOM from first principles
data.author: puzzlingcaptcha
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了HTML和DOM的局限性，并提出重新思考浏览器中的DOM模型。尽管WebAssembly取得了成功，但客户端技术自十年前以来变化不大。DOM拥有超过350个属性和660个CSS属性，且接口繁杂、遗留问题多，如`onevent`属性。大多数开发者避免直接操作DOM，而选择使用JS框架。Web Components虽然提供了原生组件功能，但因API笨重且来得太晚而不受欢迎。HTML本身的进化有限，仅在无障碍方面有所进展，而语义HTML未完全实现。CSS也变得复杂，开发者常误用其布局模型。总体而言，作者认为DOM和HTML需要重大变革以适应现代Web应用的需求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DOM、HTML、CSS的复杂性及其合理性，是否需要改革以及如何改革

不同观点：
• **支持DOM和现有Web技术**：
   - DOM和HTML虽然复杂，但这是为了保持向后兼容性和广泛的适用性（如[strogonoff]、[vlindhol]、[LauraMedia]）。
   - 复杂性是不可避免的，因为Web技术必须支持多种用例和利益相关者（如[taeric]）。
   - Web技术已经非常成功，任何改革都需要仔细考虑如何过渡（如[AshleysBrain]）。

• **批评DOM和现有Web技术**：
   - DOM和HTML过于复杂，开发者往往被不必要的抽象和复杂性困扰（如[austin-cheney]）。
   - 一些开发者对DOM有非理性的恐惧，导致不必要的技术堆叠和问题（如[austin-cheney]）。
   - 现代Web开发中，状态管理不当导致了很多问题，应该重新思考如何处理状态（如[romaniv]）。

• **建议改革或替代方案**：
   - 建议使用类似Flutter的非DOM框架，以提供更高的自由度和性能（如[socalgal2]、[lenkite]）。
   - 提议重新设计HTML，使用更灵活的标签系统（如[LauraMedia]）。
   - 提出使用Web Components或其他新的UI技术来简化开发（如[fergie]、[cyberax]）。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现和实例**：
   - 举例Google Earth使用Canvas实现复杂UI（如[socalgal2]）。
   - 讨论了Google Docs在处理表情符号和非英语输入时的困难（如[socalgal2]）。

• **争议焦点**：
   - 争议的核心在于是否应该改革现有的DOM和HTML技术，以及如何在保持兼容性的前提下进行改革（如[hungryhobbit]、[AshleysBrain]）。
   - 另一个焦点是开发者对DOM和现有技术的复杂性感受不一，部分人认为这是非理性的恐惧（如[austin-cheney]）。

• **其他值得注意的讨论点**：
   - 强调了向后兼容性的重要性和实现改革的困难（如[AshleysBrain]、[bloomca]）。
   - 讨论了Web技术的成功和其通过不断标准化适应变化的能力（如[vlindhol]）。
   - 提出了一些新的技术方向和工具，如WebGPU和Use.GPU（如[parasti]）。

总结：讨论围绕DOM和HTML的复杂性展开，有人支持现有技术的向后兼容性和广泛适用性，有人批评其复杂性和不当使用，并提出改革和替代方案。争议的焦点是如何在保持兼容性的前提下进行有效改革。

44808542.article_content:
August 06, 2025 HTML is Dead, Long Live HTML Rethinking DOM from first principles Browsers are in a very weird place. While WebAssembly has succeeded, even on the server, the client still feels largely the same as it did 10 years ago . Enthusiasts will tell you that accessing native web APIs via WASM is a solved problem, with some minimal JS glue . But the question not asked is why you would want to access the DOM. It's just the only option. So I'd like to explain why it really is time to send the DOM and its assorted APIs off to a farm somewhere, with some ideas on how. I won't pretend to know everything about browsers. Nobody knows everything anymore, and that's the problem. The 'Document' Model Few know how bad the DOM really is. In Chrome, document.body now has 350+ keys, grouped roughly like this: This doesn't include the CSS properties in document.body.style of which there are... 660 . The boundary between properties and methods is very vague. Many are just facades with an invisible setter behind them. Some getters may trigger a just-in-time re-layout. There's ancient legacy stuff, like all the onevent properties nobody uses anymore. The DOM is not lean and continues to get fatter. Whether you notice this largely depends on whether you are making web pages or web applications. Most devs now avoid working with the DOM directly, though occasionally some purist will praise pure DOM as being superior to the various JS component/templating frameworks. What little declarative facilities the DOM has, like innerHTML , do not resemble modern UI patterns at all. The DOM has too many ways to do the same thing, none of them nice. connectedCallback() { const shadow = this.attachShadow({ mode: 'closed' }), template = document.getElementById('hello-world') .content.cloneNode(true), hwMsg = `Hello ${ this.name }`; Array.from(template.querySelectorAll('.hw-text')) .forEach(n => n.textContent = hwMsg); shadow.append(template); } Web Components deserve a mention, being the web-native equivalent of JS component libraries. But they came too late and are unpopular. The API seems clunky, with its Shadow DOM introducing new nesting and scoping layers. Proponents kinda read like apologetics . The achilles heel is the DOM's SGML/XML heritage, making everything stringly typed. React-likes do not have this problem, their syntax only looks like XML. Devs have learned not to keep state in the document, because it's inadequate for it. For HTML itself, there isn't much to critique because nothing has changed in 10-15 years. Only ARIA (accessibility) is notable, and only because this was what Semantic HTML was supposed to do and didn't. Semantic HTML never quite reached its goal. Despite dating from around 2011, there is e.g. no or tag, when those were well-established idioms. Instead, an article inside an article is probably a comment. The guidelines are... weird. There's this feeling that HTML always had paper-envy, and couldn't quite embrace or fully define its hypertext nature, and did not trust its users to follow clear rules. Stewardship of HTML has since firmly passed to WHATWG, really the browser vendors, who have not been able to define anything more concrete as a vision, and have instead just added epicycles at the margins. Along the way even CSS has grown expressions, because every templating language wants to become a programming language. Editability of HTML remains a sad footnote. While technically supported via contentEditable , actually wrangling this feature into something usable for applications is a dark art. I'm sure the Google Docs and Notion people have horror stories. Nobody really believes in the old gods of progressive enhancement and separating markup from style anymore, not if they make apps. Most of the applications you see nowadays will kitbash HTML/CSS/SVG into a pretty enough shape. But this comes with immense overhead, and is looking more and more like the opposite of a decent UI toolkit. The Slack input box Off-screen clipboard hacks Lists and tables must be virtualized by hand, taking over for layout, resizing, dragging, and so on. Making a chat window's scrollbar stick to the bottom is somebody's TODO, every single time. And the more you virtualize, the more you have to reinvent find-in-page, right-click menus, etc. The web blurred the distinction between UI and fluid content, which was novel at the time. But it makes less and less sense, because the UI part is a decade obsolete, and the content has largely homogenized. CSS is inside-out CSS doesn't have a stellar reputation either, but few can put their finger on exactly why. Where most people go wrong is to start with the wrong mental model, approaching it like a constraint solver. This is easy to show with e.g.:

data.title: About the BLOBs in Ventoy
data.author: turrini
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Ventoy项目中关于BLOBs（二进制大对象）的问题。Ventoy强调其完全开源和透明性，某些二进制文件直接来自其他开源项目。作者计划通过创建GitHub子仓库并使用GitHub CI构建这些BLOBs，以提高透明度和可维护性。文中还列出了当前Ventoy源代码中的BLOBs文件，包括其来源和构建说明，并邀请社区帮助检查和完善该列表。此外，作者提出了关于GitHub是否能为FreeBSD、Windows以及不同Linux环境（glibc/musl）提供构建环境的问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ventoy软件的安全性及社区信任问题

不同观点：
• **对Ventoy安全性的严重质疑**：
   - baobun认为，即使假定维护者是诚实和善意的，他们仍然缺乏能力来确保其供应链的安全，使用Ventoy存在巨大风险。他们指出，Ventoy的安全姿态没有随着时间、威胁形势以及项目的发展而演变。
   - baobun还提出一种 cynical take，即目前的状况可能是故意表现出无知或无能，以构建合理的推诿。
   - graton表示不信任Ventoy，认为维护者在过去五年中没有对此问题做出足够回应，且对2020年提出的问题没有实质性改变，这种不作为显得可疑。

• **对Ventoy的有限信任或个人经验分享**：
   - lpcvoid表示从未信任过Ventoy，因此一直使用多个USB sticks来安装Linux系统。
   - delduca分享了自己使用Ventoy的经验，表示在大多数情况下工作良好，但无法与Arch配合使用，因此需要额外准备一个USB驱动器。

• **对Ventoy的正面评价**：
   - daft_pink表示非常喜欢Ventoy，认为其在个人homelab环境中表现出色，且不担心安全问题。

补充讨论：
• **技术性讨论**：
   - josteink指出，由于大多数人无法管理简单的dd调用，以及Windows不允许从用户空间shell直接访问物理层，导致需要更多的工作。
   
• **术语解释**：
   - immibis澄清“blob”并非首字母缩略词，而是比喻为一团无定形的物质。在数据库中，它被反向定义为“binary large object”。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于Ventoy维护者是否具备足够的技术能力和责任心来确保软件的安全性。一部分用户认为其安全姿态未能与时俱进，存在被攻击的风险，而另一部分用户则基于个人经验对其表示信任或不信任。

there are some discuss about the BLOBs in Ventoy.
For a long time, I devoted my limited spare time to adding new features and fixing bugs and didn't get around to considering this.
It should be noted firstly that Ventoy is 100% open souce and everything is transparent.
Some binary files are directly get from other open source projects and Ventoy directly use them and don't need any change by default.
Now that someone cares about these BLOBs, so I think we can discuss about this and find a better way and use it step by step in Ventoy.
This will definitely take a long time and need some help but I think it's good for Ventoy.
One approach I'm thinking of right now is that, for these BLOBs, I create some sub-repos in github and build them by github CI just once, and use the binary file in Ventoy.
If we find some problem in these tools, we can update the source code and build again and use the new binary files in new Ventoy version.
What do you think about this?
For this, I want to confirm that
Can github provide build environment for  FreeBSD and Windows ?
Can github provide build environment for Linux with glibc/musl ?
Update:  2025/05/14
Anyway, I think first step we need to get a full BLOBs list in current Ventoy source code.
Refer to

https://github.com/ventoy/Ventoy/blob/master/BLOB_List.md

44810281.article_summary: 本文讨论了Ventoy项目中关于BLOBs（二进制大对象）的问题。Ventoy强调其完全开源和透明性，某些二进制文件直接来自其他开源项目。作者计划通过创建GitHub子仓库并使用GitHub CI构建这些BLOBs，以提高透明度和可维护性。文中还列出了当前Ventoy源代码中的BLOBs文件，包括其来源和构建说明，并邀请社区帮助检查和完善该列表。此外，作者提出了关于GitHub是否能为FreeBSD、Windows以及不同Linux环境（glibc/musl）提供构建环境的问题。
44810281.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ventoy软件的安全性及社区信任问题

不同观点：
• **对Ventoy安全性的严重质疑**：
   - baobun认为，即使假定维护者是诚实和善意的，他们仍然缺乏能力来确保其供应链的安全，使用Ventoy存在巨大风险。他们指出，Ventoy的安全姿态没有随着时间、威胁形势以及项目的发展而演变。
   - baobun还提出一种 cynical take，即目前的状况可能是故意表现出无知或无能，以构建合理的推诿。
   - graton表示不信任Ventoy，认为维护者在过去五年中没有对此问题做出足够回应，且对2020年提出的问题没有实质性改变，这种不作为显得可疑。

• **对Ventoy的有限信任或个人经验分享**：
   - lpcvoid表示从未信任过Ventoy，因此一直使用多个USB sticks来安装Linux系统。
   - delduca分享了自己使用Ventoy的经验，表示在大多数情况下工作良好，但无法与Arch配合使用，因此需要额外准备一个USB驱动器。

• **对Ventoy的正面评价**：
   - daft_pink表示非常喜欢Ventoy，认为其在个人homelab环境中表现出色，且不担心安全问题。

补充讨论：
• **技术性讨论**：
   - josteink指出，由于大多数人无法管理简单的dd调用，以及Windows不允许从用户空间shell直接访问物理层，导致需要更多的工作。
   
• **术语解释**：
   - immibis澄清“blob”并非首字母缩略词，而是比喻为一团无定形的物质。在数据库中，它被反向定义为“binary large object”。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于Ventoy维护者是否具备足够的技术能力和责任心来确保软件的安全性。一部分用户认为其安全姿态未能与时俱进，存在被攻击的风险，而另一部分用户则基于个人经验对其表示信任或不信任。

data.title: NautilusTrader: Open-source algorithmic trading platform
data.author: Lwrless
data.article_summary: NautilusTrader是一个开源交易平台，提供算法交易解决方案，支持多种资产类别交易，包括加密货币、期货、股票、期权和外汇等。平台具备高性能、低延迟的执行能力，支持复杂策略的简单实现和无代码变动的实时交易。其核心组件用Rust编写，确保速度和可靠性。用户可通过Python API集成机器学习框架，利用模块化组件构建自定义策略，并通过配置快速适应不同市场和工具。Nautilus还提供纳秒级精度的时间处理和多种高级订单类型，适用于多市场无缝交易。平台开放核心代码，并提供云平台服务，助力企业优化交易操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：算法交易的可行性、难点以及与长期持有股票投资的比较

不同观点：
• jjangkke和narrator认为，没有信息优势或资金优势，交易如同抛硬币，长期来看，持有股票是最成功的投资策略。他们强调了在交易中偶尔的成功可能导致对策略的过度依赖，最终可能导致失败。
• iav和bproctor从技术角度讨论了实现算法交易的复杂性。iav指出，在量化和算法交易中，系统整合是最大的挑战，而bproctor则认为发现有效的交易策略比技术实现更困难。
• copypaper和k9294对零售交易者在算法交易中的成功机会持怀疑态度。他们指出市场变量太多，无法准确预测，且高频交易和套利策略需要极低的延迟，这对普通交易者而言几乎不可能实现。
• monkeydust和SilentM68强调了交易和投资的区别，并提出需要一个教学平台来帮助交易者在没有资本风险的情况下学习交易。
• UK-Al05和mapontosevenths对算法交易平台的实际效果持讽刺和怀疑态度，认为这些平台可能导致资金损失。
• bhasinanant和William_BB则关注合规性和性能问题，指出在高性能交易中需要满足市场法规，并关心项目的延迟和性能指标。

补充讨论：
• 对比了不同算法交易平台如LEAN engine和QuantConnect（payeurp）。
• k9294分享了在加密货币交易中的经验，强调了低延迟交易引擎的重要性，以及策略失效的现实。
• cahaya和browningstreet提出了普通用户如何从这些平台中受益的问题，并分享了个人尝试通过算法交易实现小目标的经历。

争议焦点：
• 算法交易是否适合普通零售交易者，特别是与长期持有股票相比。
• 实现高效算法交易的技术和策略发现过程中的困难，以及是否有可能通过算法交易持续盈利。

data.title: Wired Called Our AirGradient Monitor 'Not Recommended' over a Broken Display
data.author: sklargh
data.article_summary: 本文作者Achim Haug回应了《WIRED》杂志将其产品AirGradient ONE空气质量监测器标记为“不推荐”的决定。该产品曾获得多个奖项和科学认可，但因显示屏故障在《WIRED》评测中被降级。作者认为该评测不公平，指出其他推荐产品的缺陷更明显，如缺少显示屏或重要传感器，且评测缺乏明确的方法论，仅基于个人偏好。作者对评测的草率和不专业表示失望，呼吁对科技媒体评测的公正性进行反思，并强调AirGradient团队的透明、开源和以用户为中心的价值观。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对AirGradient空气监测器产品的评价是否公平，以及对产品评测的信任问题。

不同观点：
• ratelimitsteve认为评测是合理的，产品出厂时损坏且在几个月内故障是不推荐的正当理由。他强调可靠性比过多的功能更重要，并提出“开箱即坏”和“几个月内坏掉”的产品都不应被推荐。
• cinntaile认为评测对小屏幕和设备故障的批评是合理的，但将产品归入“不推荐”有点过于严厉，尤其是对小型供应商如AirGradient可能会造成较大影响。
• Jgoauh指出一些公司和其支持者在评测不佳时会攻击评测者，并提到多个类似案例，暗示这种行为是不成熟的。
• beAbU对大多数“十大产品”列表表示怀疑，认为这些评测通常与 affiliate 链接的回扣有关，不再信任网络上的产品评测。
• nati0n则持相反意见，认为AirGradient在空气监测器领域是唯一符合所有要求的竞争者，并表示对该产品的支持。
• burnt-resistor批评Wired等媒体的商业化，并认为AirGradient正在尝试做正确的事，而评测者行为苛刻且不公平。
• justusthane提出评测中加粗的关键词让阅读变得困难，属于格式问题。
• thomassmith65认为对评测的回应不够专业，建议应基于事实而非攻击记者和批评整个媒体行业。
• holografix表示不担心AirGradient的声誉，因为Wired的评测不再被信任，且AirGradient的目标用户更偏向于即插即用的群体。他个人对产品的使用体验良好。
• Havoc认为评测者只能根据手中的设备进行评测，不能因为假设不具代表性而忽视其体验。
• Workaccount2认为评测可能更多基于主观感受，而不是科学评估，并指出AirGradient比获奖产品便宜100美元，评测可能过于苛刻。
• tkdb认为开源产品在技术上更优越，但易用性和便利性不如消费级产品，并认为显示屏问题只是一个干扰点。
• rjkingan以用户身份力挺AirGradient，认为其在易用性、可修复性、开源性和数据准确性方面表现出色。
• kasajian认为功能较少的产品如果表现良好是可以接受的，但出厂损坏的产品会令人失望，并将评测的比较视为不公平。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到对评测公正性和媒体可信度的质疑，反映出对科技评测行业的普遍不信任。
• 讨论中涉及评测标准的问题，如“开箱即坏”是否应直接导致“不推荐”，以及评测者是否应考虑价格因素。
• 对AirGradient产品的具体问题如小屏幕和故障的批评，以及其开源和透明性的优势，成为争议焦点。

Achim Haug

Two weeks ago, I had what I can only describe as a

The Best Indoor Air Quality Monitors
review.
Yes, this is the same monitor that got two awards from the
AirLab micro sensor challenge
, one of the most rigorous sensor testing programs,
beating more than 30 other well known brands
. And yes, this is also the same monitor that the University of Cambridge chose -after rigorous testing- for the largest study on classroom air quality in the world. And yes, it’s the same monitor that is loved by thousands of Home Assistant users for its easy and local integration.
Today, I want to share why we feel that this is a
flawed review
and the larger picture of how influential publications’ recommendations affect manufacturers as well as consumers.
As the founder of AirGradient, many of you know that
transparency is how we operate
. This is why we are open-source and why we openly talk about our successes as well as our failures. We work closely with scientists and communities to improve air quality.
We’re often more critical of ourselves than others are, constantly raising our own bar. So when something like this happens, it feels
deeply unfair
, like when a teacher gives you an F because your pencil broke during the exam, while giving As to students who didn’t even submit their work. But let’s not get ahead of ourselves; we will explain the details below.
We’re a small team building open-source monitors, competing against companies with
massive marketing budgets and PR machines
. We started as a volunteer project in Thailand, putting impact before profit.
What we lack in marketing power, we make up for with genuine care, transparency, and authenticity. Over
50,000 users
trust our open-source approach because we believe in giving people control over their data and the ability to repair their own devices. Our monitors offer much more value at a lower price, and our competitors are probably not very happy about this.
Many companies would try to sweep this “Not Recommended” review under the rug or send lawyers. But I feel I have a responsibility here to
address this head-on
, because our community deserves to know the details, and hopefully, this will trigger a larger discussion around the integrity of tech journalism.
Now, at this point, I would really recommend that you read the
review
so that you can
form your own opinion
about it.
Why did the AirGradient One get a “Not Recommended”?
The
primary reason
cited for the “Not Recommended” label was a
failing display
on the review unit. Let me be clear: this was a legitimate hardware failure, and we take full responsibility for it. As soon as we learned about the issue, we immediately sent replacement parts and a new unit, including repair instructions, as repairability is one of our core differentiators.
However, the reviewers logic is difficult to follow when you compare it across products:
Our monitor
: Downgraded due to a faulty display (a warranty-covered hardware issue)
Another Monitor
: Recommended, despite having
no display at all
Another Monitor
: Also recommended, despite
lacking a CO2 sensor
âone of the most critical metrics for assessing indoor air quality and ventilation
How can a product be penalized for a failing display when another recommended product has no display? How can an indoor monitor without CO2 sensing - essential for understanding indoor air quality - be recommended over one that includes this crucial measurement?
If the author had reached out regarding the failing display (a single unit from any brand can fail - even those known for high quality) and noted that their first unit failed in the final review, we would understand. But to fail the whole unit on what we know is an isolated issue feels very unfair.
However, what’s
most shocking
for me is that this review is labelled as “The Best Indoor Air Quality Monitors”, yet it has
basically no testing methodology at all
and is pretty much purely based on the personal preferences of the author.
The icing on the cake is that I actually corresponded with the author about the issues and sent detailed explanations of our methodology concerns. The responses I got back were limited to brief acknowledgements like “Received. I’m on deadline for three other stories and cannot give you a timeline.”
This response encapsulates many things wrong with the current state of tech journalism: recommendations that affect
livelihoods and purchasing decisions
are treated as just deadlines to meet, not as professional evaluations that deserve

data.article_summary: Automerge 3.0 大幅降低了内存使用，特别是在处理具有长历史的文档时，内存消耗减少了10倍以上。这使得它在更多场景下变得可行。新版本在运行时使用压缩格式，显著节省了内存，例如将《白鲸》文本粘贴到文档中，内存消耗从700MB降至1.3MB。此外，加载大型文档的速度也大大提升。API方面，清理了冗余接口，特别是文本处理部分，现在默认使用协作式字符串，并移除了旧的Text API，改用ImmutableString代表非协作式文本。新版本与之前文件格式兼容，建议用户升级。

44777086.article_content:
Automerge is a local-first data sync engine that makes it easy to build collaborative apps. Today we're excited to announce version 3.0 of Automerge!
The main update is a dramatic reduction in memory usage. Automerge stores the full history of documents to facilitate offline collaboration and version control workflows; in previous versions of the library, this could lead to gigabytes of memory usage when working with documents that had long histories. Now, in Automerge 3.0,
we've cut that down memory usage by over 10x
, sometimes dramatically more, making Automerge feasible to use in a much wider range of scenarios.
In addition to the memory usage improvements, we've also cleaned up some redundant APIs, particularly around the dealing with text strings.
If you're using Automerge already, you should upgrade today. Automerge 3.0 uses the same file format as Automerge 2 and the API is nearly fully backwards compatible. See
the migration guide
for more details.
If you're not using Automerge yet, now's a great time to take another look, as things have come a long way in performance and reliability.
To learn more about how we achieved these improvements, read on.
Improved Memory Use
​
Automerge is a data sync engine. As an application developer you work with plain-old-JavaScript-objects and Automerge takes care of persistence, and networking. Unlike most sync engines, Automerge is designed for local-first applications, which means that we need to support working offline, or using multiple independent sync servers, or not having a server at all and doing everything peer-to-peer.
Automerge achieves local first sync by storing every change you make to a document and then when concurrent changes are made - as they will be in a local-first application - we can provide good version control tools for detecting conflicts and reviewing history.  The downside is that we have to store a lot of metadata about changes - we assign a unique ID to every keystroke for example. Most of the technical work in Automerge is making it possible to store and manipulate these increasingly large histories.
Previous versions of Automerge already used a compressed columnar format to store and transmit this metadata. This format achieved a reasonably small metadata overhead "at rest" —  over the raw data for most documents. However, when a document was actually
loaded
for editing, we used an uncompressed format for the history, so the memory usage would balloon to a significantly larger overhead.
In Automerge 3.0, we've rearchitected the library so that it also uses the compressed representation at runtime. This has achieved huge memory savings. For example, pasting Moby Dick into an Automerge 2 document consumes 700Mb of memory, in Automerge 3 it only consumes 1.3Mb!
Beyond the obvious benefits of avoiding high memory usage on client devices, we've also seen that reduced memory usage can make it easier to reliably operate busy sync servers that can hold many large documents in memory at once.
Finally, for documents with large histories load times can be much much faster (we recently had an example of a document which hadn't loaded after 17 hours loading in 9 seconds!).
API Paper Cuts
​
We've also cleaned up several APIs in this release, particularly around handling text.
Automerge can manage two kinds of strings: "collaborative strings" that can merge edits from multiple users, and "non-collaborative strings" where edits from different users cannot be merged.
In Automerge 1.0, we used native JavaScript strings to represent non-collaborative strings, and a special
Text
class to represent collaborative strings. In Automerge 2.0, we released an experimental API under the
next
namespace, making collaborative text the default case—using
string
s to represent collaborative text, and a special
RawString
class to represent the less common case of non-collaborative text.
In Automerge 3.0, we're fully committing to the new API—we've removed the
Text
API, and made the
next
API the default behavior of the library. (We've also renamed
RawString
to
ImmutableString
as a more descriptive name.)
Try it out
​
Automerge 3.0 is used by default when installing the latest version (
2.1.0
) of
@automerge/automerge-repo
or
@automerge/react
. If you're new to automerge take a look at the
tutorial
to get started.
If you already have an Automerge codebase take a look at the
migration guide
to see if you need to change anything other than the version number of Automerge you depend on. If you just depend on
@automerge/automerge-repo
you'll need to run
npm update @automerge/automerge
(or your package manager's equivalent) to pull in the new version.
If things aren't working, please
create an issue
or if you have questions
join our Discord
.

data.title: Breaking the sorting barrier for directed single-source shortest paths
data.author: baruchel
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了一种突破经典算法速度限制的新方法，用于解决计算机科学中的最短路径问题。传统的最短路径算法，如1956年Edsger Dijkstra提出的算法，通过逐步扩展已探索区域来找到从起点到其他所有节点的最短路径。然而，由于最终结果需要排序，这种方法受限于“排序障碍”，无法进一步提升速度。

过去的研究在特定条件下打破了这一障碍，但对任意权重的图仍然无解。直到2021年，清华大学的段然提出了一种新算法，成功打破了排序障碍。该算法的关键在于每一步选择下一个探索节点的策略，避免了排序过程，从而提高了速度。这一成果被视为计算机科学领域的重大突破。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新算法复杂度及其在图算法中的应用

不同观点：
• [o11c] 认为该算法在高度密集图中的表现会更复杂，尤其是当边的数量 `m` 远大于节点数量 `n` 时。他还指出，对于某些图类型（如开放网格图），Dijkstra算法中的前线节点数量是有限的（如`sqrt(n)`），并且提到非基于比较的排序方法（如桶排序）可能在这种算法中更有效。

• [karussell] 关注该算法在社区中的传播，指出这个算法经过多次提交才引起更广泛的关注，带有一定的幽默感。

• [polytely] 对该算法的发现过程表示赞叹，认为这种算法虽然看起来可能在游戏开发中偶然发现，但实际上其发现过程非常了不起。

• [ljlolel] 提到其算法教授Tarjan，并指出Tarjan发明了许多算法，暗示对新算法的创造性持保留态度。

• [aDyslecticCrow] 觉得文章过于冗长且细节不足，期待论文中更详细的描述，并关心新算法如何保证Dijkstra所能提供的“全局最小值”，担心前线节点的聚集可能会导致遗漏某些解。

• [flafla2] 对新算法的复杂度O(m log^2/3 n)表示赞叹，认为这是一个巨大的成就。

• [ape4] 认为新算法比Dijkstra算法复杂得多，但这是算法发展的自然趋势。

• [crawfordcomeaux] 提出将该算法与随机性结合使用，以进一步加快算法的可能性。

补充讨论：
• 不同用户对算法复杂度的关注点不同，有的关注数学和复杂度分析（如[o11c], [flafla2]），有的则关心算法的实际应用和潜在改进（如[crawfordcomeaux], [aDyslecticCrow]）。
• 对新算法的发现和传播也有一定的讨论，[karussell]和[polytely]对此表现出一定的兴趣和感慨。
• 争议焦点在于新算法是否能在所有情况下替代Dijkstra，尤其是关于“全局最小值”的保证和前线节点处理的潜在问题([aDyslecticCrow])。

New Method Is the Fastest Way To Find the Best Routes
By
Ben Brubaker
August 6, 2025
A canonical problem in computer science is to find the shortest route to every point in a network. A new approach beats the classic algorithm taught in textbooks.
Comment
Save Article
Read Later
DVDP for
Quanta Magazine
Introduction
By
Ben Brubaker
Staff Writer
August 6, 2025
View PDF/Print Mode
algorithms
computer science
graph theory
networks
All topics
If you want to solve a tricky problem, it often helps to get organized. You might, for example, break the problem into pieces and tackle the easiest pieces first. But this kind of sorting has a cost. You may end up spending too much time putting the pieces in order.
This dilemma is especially relevant to one of the most iconic problems in computer science: finding the shortest path from a specific starting point in a network to every other point. It’s like a souped-up version of a problem you need to solve each time you move: learning the best route from your new home to work, the gym and the supermarket.
“Shortest-paths is a beautiful problem that anyone in the world can relate to,” said
Mikkel Thorup
, a computer scientist at the University of Copenhagen.
Intuitively, it should be easiest to find the shortest path to nearby destinations. So if you want to design the fastest possible algorithm for the shortest-paths problem, it seems reasonable to start by finding the closest point, then the next-closest, and so on. But to do that, you need to repeatedly figure out which point is closest. You’ll sort the points by distance as you go. There’s a fundamental speed limit for any algorithm that follows this approach: You can’t go any faster than the time it takes to sort.
Forty years ago, researchers designing shortest-paths algorithms ran up against this “sorting barrier.” Now, a team of researchers has devised
a new algorithm that breaks it
. It doesn’t sort, and it runs faster than any algorithm that does.
“The authors were audacious in thinking they could break this barrier,” said
Robert Tarjan
, a computer scientist at Princeton University. “It’s an amazing result.”
The Frontier of Knowledge
To analyze the shortest-paths problem mathematically, researchers use the language of graphs — networks of points, or nodes, connected by lines. Each link between nodes is labeled with a number called its weight, which can represent the length of that segment or the time needed to traverse it. There are usually many routes between any two nodes, and the shortest is the one whose weights add up to the smallest number. Given a graph and a specific “source” node, an algorithm’s goal is to find the shortest path to every other node.
The
most famous shortest-paths algorithm
,
devised
by the pioneering computer scientist Edsger Dijkstra in 1956, starts at the source and works outward step by step. It’s an effective approach because knowing the shortest path to nearby nodes can help you find the shortest paths to more distant ones. But because the end result is a sorted list of shortest paths, the sorting barrier sets a fundamental limit on how fast the algorithm can run.
Mark Belan, Samuel Velasco/
Quanta Magazine
In 1984, Tarjan and another researcher
improved Dijkstra’s original algorithm
so that it hit this speed limit. Any further improvement would have to come from an algorithm that avoids sorting.
In the late 1990s and early 2000s, Thorup and other researchers devised algorithms that broke the sorting barrier, but they needed to make
certain
assumptions
about weights. Nobody knew how to extend their techniques to arbitrary weights. It seemed they’d hit the end of the road.
“The research stopped for a very long time,” said
Ran Duan
, a computer scientist at Tsinghua University in Beijing. “Many people believed that there’s no better way.”

文章介绍了一种突破经典算法速度限制的新方法，用于解决计算机科学中的最短路径问题。传统的最短路径算法，如1956年Edsger Dijkstra提出的算法，通过逐步扩展已探索区域来找到从起点到其他所有节点的最短路径。然而，由于最终结果需要排序，这种方法受限于“排序障碍”，无法进一步提升速度。

过去的研究在特定条件下打破了这一障碍，但对任意权重的图仍然无解。直到2021年，清华大学的段然提出了一种新算法，成功打破了排序障碍。该算法的关键在于每一步选择下一个探索节点的策略，避免了排序过程，从而提高了速度。这一成果被视为计算机科学领域的重大突破。

不同观点：
• [o11c] 认为该算法在高度密集图中的表现会更复杂，尤其是当边的数量 `m` 远大于节点数量 `n` 时。他还指出，对于某些图类型（如开放网格图），Dijkstra算法中的前线节点数量是有限的（如`sqrt(n)`），并且提到非基于比较的排序方法（如桶排序）可能在这种算法中更有效。

• [karussell] 关注该算法在社区中的传播，指出这个算法经过多次提交才引起更广泛的关注，带有一定的幽默感。

• [polytely] 对该算法的发现过程表示赞叹，认为这种算法虽然看起来可能在游戏开发中偶然发现，但实际上其发现过程非常了不起。

• [ljlolel] 提到其算法教授Tarjan，并指出Tarjan发明了许多算法，暗示对新算法的创造性持保留态度。

• [aDyslecticCrow] 觉得文章过于冗长且细节不足，期待论文中更详细的描述，并关心新算法如何保证Dijkstra所能提供的“全局最小值”，担心前线节点的聚集可能会导致遗漏某些解。

• [flafla2] 对新算法的复杂度O(m log^2/3 n)表示赞叹，认为这是一个巨大的成就。

• [ape4] 认为新算法比Dijkstra算法复杂得多，但这是算法发展的自然趋势。

• 对新算法的发现和传播也有一定的讨论，[karussell]和[polytely]对此表现出一定的兴趣和感慨。

data.title: Dotfiles feel too personal to share
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了作者对分享dotfiles（软件配置文件）的复杂情感。虽然作者喜欢配置和使用dotfiles，并从中获得效率，但觉得这些个性化设置过于私密，不愿公开分享。作者平常乐于分享自己的想法和代码，但dotfiles让他感到不适。他的dotfiles包含zsh、tmux、neovim等配置，使用GNU Stow管理，确保多台设备同步。尽管拥有完善的配置库，他仍选择暂时不公开，期待未来能更自在地分享。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕是否分享 dotfiles 以及如何分享 dotfiles 的讨论，涉及个性化配置、隐私与安全、以及分享的文化。

不同观点：
• **实用性与可移植性优先**：[justonceokay] 认为过度依赖自定义插件和配置会让在无配置环境下的操作变得麻烦。他主张在分享 dotfiles 时，尽量使用默认配置以提高兼容性，并引用禅语强调适应默认配置的价值。

• **分享文化与隐私的平衡**：[alisonatwork] 支持默认分享的文化，认为从他人配置中学习是有价值的，但也意识到在工作环境中共享配置可能涉及敏感信息，因此对如何平衡分享与隐私有疑虑。

• **语言与工具讨论**：[wlindley] 对评论中的语法错误提出批评，认为讨论应该更严谨，尤其是在技术讨论中。

• **加密与隐私保护**：[kernc] 认为有些配置过于私密，不应分享，并开发了工具 myba 来加密同步配置文件。他强调有些信息应该保密。

• **选择性分享工具的推荐**：[twp] 提出可以使用工具如 chezmoi 来精确控制哪些配置可以分享，哪些需要保密，如使用加密技术保护敏感信息。

• **敏感信息暴露的风险**：[lrvick] 从安全研究者的角度分析了暴露 dotfiles 的潜在风险，尤其是如果配置中显示使用不安全的包管理器或允许远程代码执行。他建议对敏感工作环境进行物理隔离以减少风险。

• **对分享的开放态度**：[nobleach] 和 [incognito124] 表示他们乐于分享自己的配置，认为这有助于他人学习，同时也提到他们会对工作相关的特定配置进行保护。

• **不分享的立场**：[sodapopcan] 表示不理解为什么不分享 dotfiles，认为通过简单的方法可以有效保护隐私，并从他人配置中学到很多。

补充讨论：
• **工具与解决方案**：多位评论者提到使用 chezmoi 等工具来实现选择性分享和加密，以应对隐私和安全问题。
• **社会工程学风险**：[jacobsenscott] 指出，即使没有明显的秘密信息，dotfiles 也可能被用于社会工程学攻击，因此需要谨慎处理。
• **长期实践分享**：[alexandroqc] 和 [CMCDragonkai] 分享了他们长期公开 dotfiles 的经验，并推荐使用工具如 Polykey 来管理秘密信息。

争议焦点：
• 分享 dotfiles 的价值与风险：部分评论者认为分享有助于社区学习，而另一些人则担心隐私泄露和安全风险。
• 默认配置与自定义配置的平衡：有些人主张尽量使用默认配置以提高兼容性，而另一些人则强调个性化配置的重要性。

总结：讨论围绕 dotfiles 分享的利弊、隐私保护的方法、以及个性化与默认配置的取舍展开，涉及实用性、安全性和分享文化等多方面问题。

44812611.article_content:
Dotfiles feel too intimate and personal to share
Aug 6th, 2025
by
Juha-Matti Santala
(
Mastodon
@hamatti@hamatti.org
)
This was published in categories:
blaugust
blaugust-2025
dev
documentation
I
love
dotfiles.
“Dotfiles” is a term that refers to configuration files used to configure
software and operating systems. They are called such because often these files
start with a dot. You may have seen
.bashrc
,
.tmux.conf
or
.zshrc
in the wild.
Whenever a software doesn’t offer direct file-based configuration, I feel sad
because it means I need to take extra steps to keep my configuration across
different devices in sync or when setting up a new machine.
I
love
sharing.
I regularly publish ideas and experiences in
my blog
, I share my notes in
my digital garden
and I publish almost all the code I write (outside work) as open source
in GitHub
.
I
love
to read
other people’s dotfiles
and learn from them.
Yet, somehow I feel like sharing my own dotfiles to the world is beyond my
comfort zone. I feel my customisations and aliases and other decisions are too
intimate and personal to share.
I don’t quite know why though.
I have a really cool repository where I keep my dotfiles and there’s quite a
lot there. There’s the usual suspects like my
zsh
config and aliases, my
tmux
configuration and my
neovim
and
vscode
stuff too. And my
Python startup script
.
I also keep my
Homebrew
core list
there: that’s all the packages I want to always have at hand. Having them all
in one place to be installed with a single command on a new computer is
lovely.
I also keep my
Stylus
CSS rules there so I can easily bring the experience I want on any browser I
use.
I use
GNU Stow to manage most of these
. For anything that’s directly applicable by copying the files into a given
folder, I’ve set up the folder structure so that running
stow [folder]
will create symlinks to
right places: any change made into the repository from any machine will apply
to all machines. It’s so cool.
All in all, my dotfiles repository is home to 19 configuration files +
everything my neovim installation has, plugins and all.
For now however, I
keep them secret, keep them safe
until I
feel better about sharing my dotfiles with the world.
If something above resonated with you, let's start a discussion about it!
Email me at juhamattisantala at gmail dot com and share your thoughts
. In 2025, I want to have more deeper discussions with people from around the world and I'd love if you'd be part of that.

data.title: Claude Code IDE integration for Emacs
data.author: kgwgk
data.article_summary: Claude Code IDE for Emacs 通过 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 实现与 Claude Code CLI 的原生集成，构建了 Claude 与 Emacs 之间的双向桥梁。该工具使 Claude 能够利用 Emacs 的强大功能，如 LSP、项目管理及自定义 Elisp 函数，从而成为真正的 Emacs 感知 AI 助手。主要功能包括自动项目检测、终端集成、MCP 协议支持、工具扩展服务器、诊断集成、高级差异查看、标签栏支持及选择和缓冲区跟踪。通过与 LSP、Tree-sitter、Imenu 和项目管理集成，Claude 可以执行项目内搜索、重构及调用自定义 Elisp 函数。安装需 Emacs 28.1 及以上版本和 Claude Code CLI，并通过 `use-package` 进行配置。基本使用通过交互菜单 `M-x claude-code-ide-menu` 实现。

Claude Code IDE for Emacs
Overview
Claude Code IDE for Emacs provides native integration with Claude Code CLI through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Unlike simple terminal wrappers, this package creates a bidirectional bridge between Claude and Emacs, enabling Claude to understand and leverage Emacs’ powerful features—from LSP and project management to custom Elisp functions. This transforms Claude into a true Emacs-aware AI assistant that works within your existing workflow and can interact with your entire Emacs ecosystem.
Features
Automatic project detection and session management
Terminal integration with full color support using
vterm
or
eat
MCP protocol implementation for IDE integration
Tool support for file operations, editor state, and workspace info
Extensible MCP tools server for accessing Emacs commands (xrefs, tree-sitter, project info, e.g.)
Diagnostic integration with Flycheck and Flymake
Advanced diff view with ediff integration
Tab-bar support for proper context switching

data.title: Google suffers data breach in ongoing Salesforce data theft attacks
data.author: mikece
data.article_summary: Google近日证实，在今年6月成为ShinyHunters黑客组织针对Salesforce客户关系管理（CRM）系统数据盗窃攻击的受害者。攻击者通过语音钓鱼（vishing）诈骗获取员工信息，入侵Salesforce实例并窃取客户数据，试图勒索公司支付赎金以防止数据泄露。被盗数据包括中小企业的基础联系信息，多为公开可获取的数据。ShinyHunters已进行多次类似攻击，目标包括Adidas、Qantas、Cisco等公司，部分公司已支付赎金以避免数据泄露。攻击者还计划在私下的勒索结束后，将数据公开或在黑客论坛上出售。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google使用Salesforce系统时发生数据泄露事件，参与者讨论了数据泄露的原因、影响以及Google为何使用第三方客户管理系统而非自建系统。

不同观点：
• [kyrra & GHanku] 引用的文章指出，数据泄露涉及威胁行为者通过Salesforce Data Loader获取中小企业联系信息和相关笔记。泄露的数据包括基本的公开业务信息，如企业名称和联系方式。GHanku进一步解释了攻击者如何通过社会工程学手段，诱骗员工连接到恶意的Data Loader应用以导出数据，并利用这些数据访问其他云平台。

• [cjonas] 猜测泄露可能源于force.com网站的配置错误，这种配置错误允许公开访问基本业务信息。他提到这种问题在过去很常见，尽管Salesforce已经发布了许多安全补丁，但大多需要管理员手动操作才能生效。他还指出，这种漏洞广泛存在，但奇怪的是没有引起媒体关注。

• [Bluescreenbuddy & grumple] 对Google为何不开发自己的内部客户管理系统表示惊讶，认为Google似乎没有销售人员或客户管理需求，使用Salesforce显得不寻常。

• [ok123456] 提出了此次事件是否与AI生成内容有关的猜测，链接了一篇关于AI撰写销售材料的文章，但未展开讨论具体关联。

• [wferrell] 解释了Google内部CRM系统存在的问题，指出其有缺陷且工程师不愿意维护，暗示使用Salesforce可能是出于无奈。

• [mrweasel] 联想到自己经历的数据丢失事件，怀疑是否与KLM的数据泄露有关，但未提供具体证据。

• [shadowgovt] 对Google使用Salesforce表示理解，指出Google通过收购快速扩展，可能继承了被收购公司的系统。他还提到Google内部对开发Salesforce替代品的兴趣不大，因为员工认为这样的工作枯燥乏味。

• [01HNNWZ0MV43FF] 简短地评论了数据泄露事件的影响，指出最终受害者是用户，并用幽默链接了一首歌曲。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对Salesforce配置错误导致数据泄露的技术细节，以及Google为何选择使用第三方系统而非自建系统的原因分析。
• 参与者还提到了攻击者如何利用社会工程学手段获取数据，以及Google内部CRM系统存在的缺陷和工程师对维护这些系统的抵触情绪。
• 争议的焦点在于Google这样的大公司为何依赖第三方客户管理系统，以及在数据安全和系统维护上的责任归属。

44812198.article_content:
Google suffers data breach in ongoing Salesforce data theft attacks
By
Lawrence Abrams
August 6, 2025
09:51 AM
0
Google is the latest company to suffer a data breach in an ongoing wave of Salesforce CRM data theft attacks conducted by the ShinyHunters extortion group.
In June,
Google warned
that a threat actor they classify as 'UNC6040' is targeting companies' employees in voice phishing (vishing) social engineering attacks to breach Salesforce instances and download customer data. This data is then used to extort companies into paying a ransom to prevent the data from being leaked.
In a brief update to the article last night, Google said that it too fell victim to the same attack in June after one of its Salesforce CRM instances was breached and customer data was stolen.
"In June, one of Google's corporate Salesforce instances was impacted by similar UNC6040 activity described in this post. Google responded to the activity, performed an impact analysis and began mitigations,"
reads Google's update
.
"The instance was used to store contact information and related notes for small and medium businesses. Analysis revealed that data was retrieved by the threat actor during a small window of time before the access was cut off."
"The data retrieved by the threat actor was confined to basic and largely publicly available business information, such as business names and contact details."
Google is classifying the threat actors behind these attacks as 'UNC6040' or 'UNC6240.' However, BleepingComputer, which has been tracking these attacks, has learned that a notorious threat actor known as
ShinyHunters is behind the attacks
.
ShinyHunters has been around for years, responsible for a wide range of breaches, including those at
PowerSchool
,
Oracle Cloud
, the
Snowflake data-theft attacks
,
AT&T
,
NitroPDF
,
Wattpad
,
MathWay
, and
many more
.
In a conversation with BleepingComputer yesterday, ShinyHunters claimed to have breached many Salesforce instances, with attacks still ongoing.
The threat actor claimed yesterday to BleepingComputer that they breached a trillion-dollar company, and were considering just leaking the data rather than attempting to extort them. It is unclear if this company is Google.
As for the other companies impacted in these attacks, the threat actor is extorting them through email, demanding they pay a ransom to prevent the data from being publicly leaked.
Once the threat actor has finished privately extorting companies, they plan to publicly leak or sell data on a hacking forum.
BleepingComputer has learned of one company that has already paid 4 Bitcoins, or approximately $400,000, to prevent the leak of their data.
Other companies impacted in these attacks include
Adidas
,
Qantas
,
Allianz Life
,
Cisco
, and the LVMH subsidiaries
Louis Vuitton
,
Dior
, and
Tiffany & Co.

data.title: The 1090 Megahertz Riddle: A Guide to Decoding Mode S and ADS-B Signals
data.author: toomuchtodo
data.article_summary: 《1090兆赫之谜：Mode S和ADS-B信号解码指南》由代尔夫特理工大学的Junzi Sun撰写，介绍了飞机从控制器询问向自动广播的转变。ADS-B（自动相关监视广播）是飞机报告状态信息（如身份、位置和速度）的常用方法，利用1090兆赫的 transponder 传输数据。本书系统地讲解了Mode S和ADS-B数据的解码过程，涵盖了基础知识（如初級雷達、次級雷達、Mode S等）、硬件和软件设置，以及如何使用Python代码进行信号解码。全书详细解析了各类ADS-B信号和常用Mode S信号，并为研究人员和爱好者提供了研究方向的总结。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕《The 1090 Megahertz Riddle》这本书及其相关ADS-B和Mode S数据的讨论

不同观点：
• [toomuchtodo] 认为，本书填补了航空器监视领域的一大空白，系统地介绍了ADS-B和Mode S数据的解码过程，并为研究人员、工程师和爱好者提供了详细的指导。特别指出了书中包含的大量背景知识、硬件和软件设置说明，以及丰富的Python代码示例。

• [CoolNamesAllTkn] 赞扬本书是一个很好的参考资源，并提到作者Junzi将内容发布在网站上，提供了比昂贵的DO-260标准文档更实惠的选择。他还分享了自己在开源ADS-B接收器项目中的使用经验，特别是在RP2040 PIO上解码Mode S信号。

• [yubiox] 提到有关pingGPS便携式ADS-B接收器重新有货的消息，这对想要购买此类设备的用户是一个有用的信息更新。

• [Catbert59] 指出ADS-B数据在气象学中的应用潜力，例如提取风数据，以及用于定位GPS干扰区域，因为ADS-B可以在GPS接收失败时通过惯性后备机制传输位置信息。

• [willwade] 提供了有关接收ADS-B信号所需硬件的信息，并分享了一个购买RTL-SDR设备的链接，为新手提供了实用的入门指导。

• [runlaszlorun] 幽默地提到Elon Musk（可能与SpaceX或Tesla相关）对ADS-B敏感的问题，暗示有人可能因住在机场附近而对ADS-B信号感兴趣，并提到自己拥有多个rtl-sdr设备。

• [tiagod] 对书中关于PSR（主监视雷达）描述的准确性提出质疑，认为应使用方向性天线而非全向天线，属于技术性讨论。

补充讨论：
• [jjwiseman] 简单评价本书，并纠正了书籍标题为"The 1090 Megahertz Riddle"，而非之前提到的其他名称。
• [jasonjayr] 提到之前在另一个讨论中已经涉及过基于ADS-B数据的天气模型，并认为这本书非常全面，链接到了之前的讨论。

争议焦点：
• [tiagod] 对书中技术描述的准确性提出质疑，特别是关于PSR天线类型的描述，引发对技术细节的讨论。

整体来看，讨论围绕本书的技术内容、实际应用、硬件设备以及相关技术挑战展开，参与者分享了各自的见解和相关资源。

44778772.article_content:
The 1090 Megahertz Riddle: A Guide to Decoding Mode S and ADS-B Signals
Authors
Junzi Sun
Department of Control and Operations, Faculty of Aerospace Engineering, Delft University of Technology, The Netherlands
https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3888-1192
DOI:
https://doi.org/10.34641/mg.11
Keywords:
Aircraft Surveillance, 											Decoding, 											Mode S, 											ADS-B, 											Open data, 											pyModeS
Synopsis
In the last twenty years, aircraft surveillance has moved from controller-based interrogation to automatic broadcast. The Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) is one of the most common methods for aircraft to report their state information like identity, position, and speed. Like other Mode S communications, ADS-B makes use of the 1090 megahertz transponder to transmit data. The protocol for ADS-B is open, and low-cost receivers can easily be used to intercept its signals. Many recent air transportation studies have benefited from this open data source. However, the current literature does not offer a systematic exploration of Mode S and ADS-B data, nor does it explain the decoding process.
This book tackles this missing area in the literature. It offers researchers, engineers, and enthusiasts a clear guide to understanding and making use of open ADS-B and Mode S data. The first part of this book presents the knowledge required to get started with decoding these signals. It includes background information on primary radar, secondary radar, Mode A/C, Mode S, and ADS-B, as well as the hardware and software setups necessary to gather radio signals. After that, the 17 core chapters of the book investigate the details of all types of ADS-B signals and commonly used Mode S signals. Throughout these chapters, examples and sample Python code are used extensively to explain and demonstrate the decoding process. Finally, the last chapter of the book offers a summary and a brief overview of research topics that go beyond the decoding of these signals.
Downloads
Download data is not yet available.
Author Biography
Junzi Sun,
Department of Control and Operations, Faculty of Aerospace Engineering, Delft University of Technology, The Netherlands
Junzi Sun is an assistant professor at TU Delft, currently working in the CNS/ATM group of the Aerospace Engineering Faculty. He is passionate about open-source, open science, and making air transportation more sustainable.
He was born in China and completed his bachelor’s degree in telecommunication at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications. Then, he moved to Europe and obtained his master’s degree in aerospace engineering at Polytechnic University of Catalonia. After that, he worked in Spain and France for a few years before continuing his doctoral research in the Netherlands, where he obtained his Ph.D. degree and currently works and lives.

44778772.article_summary: 《1090兆赫之谜：Mode S和ADS-B信号解码指南》由代尔夫特理工大学的Junzi Sun撰写，介绍了飞机从控制器询问向自动广播的转变。ADS-B（自动相关监视广播）是飞机报告状态信息（如身份、位置和速度）的常用方法，利用1090兆赫的 transponder 传输数据。本书系统地讲解了Mode S和ADS-B数据的解码过程，涵盖了基础知识（如初級雷達、次級雷達、Mode S等）、硬件和软件设置，以及如何使用Python代码进行信号解码。全书详细解析了各类ADS-B信号和常用Mode S信号，并为研究人员和爱好者提供了研究方向的总结。
44778772.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕《The 1090 Megahertz Riddle》这本书及其相关ADS-B和Mode S数据的讨论

不同观点：
• [toomuchtodo] 认为，本书填补了航空器监视领域的一大空白，系统地介绍了ADS-B和Mode S数据的解码过程，并为研究人员、工程师和爱好者提供了详细的指导。特别指出了书中包含的大量背景知识、硬件和软件设置说明，以及丰富的Python代码示例。

• [CoolNamesAllTkn] 赞扬本书是一个很好的参考资源，并提到作者Junzi将内容发布在网站上，提供了比昂贵的DO-260标准文档更实惠的选择。他还分享了自己在开源ADS-B接收器项目中的使用经验，特别是在RP2040 PIO上解码Mode S信号。

• [yubiox] 提到有关pingGPS便携式ADS-B接收器重新有货的消息，这对想要购买此类设备的用户是一个有用的信息更新。

• [Catbert59] 指出ADS-B数据在气象学中的应用潜力，例如提取风数据，以及用于定位GPS干扰区域，因为ADS-B可以在GPS接收失败时通过惯性后备机制传输位置信息。

• [willwade] 提供了有关接收ADS-B信号所需硬件的信息，并分享了一个购买RTL-SDR设备的链接，为新手提供了实用的入门指导。

• [runlaszlorun] 幽默地提到Elon Musk（可能与SpaceX或Tesla相关）对ADS-B敏感的问题，暗示有人可能因住在机场附近而对ADS-B信号感兴趣，并提到自己拥有多个rtl-sdr设备。

• [tiagod] 对书中关于PSR（主监视雷达）描述的准确性提出质疑，认为应使用方向性天线而非全向天线，属于技术性讨论。

补充讨论：
• [jjwiseman] 简单评价本书，并纠正了书籍标题为"The 1090 Megahertz Riddle"，而非之前提到的其他名称。
• [jasonjayr] 提到之前在另一个讨论中已经涉及过基于ADS-B数据的天气模型，并认为这本书非常全面，链接到了之前的讨论。

争议焦点：
• [tiagod] 对书中技术描述的准确性提出质疑，特别是关于PSR天线类型的描述，引发对技术细节的讨论。

整体来看，讨论围绕本书的技术内容、实际应用、硬件设备以及相关技术挑战展开，参与者分享了各自的见解和相关资源。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个未完成的网页音乐工具的评论，涉及功能建议、技术问题、使用体验以及对电子音乐的热爱。

不同观点：
• [errozero] 提到该工具未完成，并表示打算为Firefox添加一个polyfill来解决缺失的`cancelAndHoldAtTime`函数问题，随后进行了临时的修复。
• [driggs] 对该工具的音乐性和技术实现表示赞赏，尤其是其三个TB-303合成引擎和自动生成的多节奏模式，认为这是一个在浏览器中运行的优秀工具。
• [nzoschke] 喜欢该工具的用户界面风格，并分享了类似的音乐工具链接，还提到了一个与303相关的音乐活动。
• [bityard] 对303有深厚感情，分享了自己的使用经历，并表示该工具激发了他重新投入电子音乐创作的兴趣。
• [octatrack] 喜欢该工具，但建议增加MIDI同步和启动/停止功能，以便与其他设备/软件连接。
• [bitbasher] 询问如何进入电子音乐制作领域，分享了自己使用Renoise的经验，并寻求更多建议。
• [ZFH] 表示该工具唤起了对Propellerhead Rebirth的怀旧情感。
• [kookamamie] 建议在重新生成序列时保持当前播放状态，如果此时播放状态是激活的话。
• [andreyazimov] 请求添加一个简单的909鼓组。
• [xxr] 提到该工具生成的音乐风格类似于Frank Klepacki在Red Alert 2原声带中的作品。
• [serpent] 询问该工具的源代码是否公开。
• [quatonion] 对该工具的生成机制表示赞赏，并建议写一篇文章详细介绍。
• [mxuribe] 提到在ungoogled chromium中使用该工具时，点击停止按钮后仍然有低音量播放或回声的问题，但多次点击最终能停止播放，并对工具的概念表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• [peterldowns] 提到该工具在Firefox中无法正常工作，控制台报错`cancelAndHoldAtTime`函数不存在，但在Chrome中运行良好。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在工具在不同浏览器中的兼容性问题，特别是Firefox中函数缺失的问题。
• 功能上的改进建议较多，比如MIDI同步、播放状态保持等，显示出用户对该工具进一步完善的期待。

data.title: Show HN: An open-source e-book reader for conversational reading with an LLM
data.author: takigon
data.article_summary: BookWith是一个创新的电子书阅读平台，利用AI技术提升阅读体验。与传统电子书阅读器不同，BookWith通过实时对话帮助读者解答疑问、加深理解，并将当前阅读内容与过去的阅读材料自动关联。其主要功能包括：AI阅读助手，能根据上下文提供即时答案和深入见解；AI播客生成，将书本内容转化为对话式播客；多层次记忆系统，确保阅读的连贯性；智能标注，通过不同颜色高亮和智能笔记增强理解。平台支持日语和英语，提供个性化阅读体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在阅读和解析书籍内容中的应用及其潜在价值和问题

不同观点：
• nerdjon：认为使用LLM工具阅读书籍可能导致注意力持续下降的问题，并担心AI无法确保提供准确的信息。他质疑使用这种工具的必要性，认为这是对阅读能力的依赖性增强的表现。
• patcon：认为LLM工具可以帮助那些拥有深厚知识但写作能力不足的人分享他们的智慧，特别是在处理结构不良但内容正确的书籍时。
• spudlyo：分享了个人使用LLM工具阅读经典文学作品的积极经验，通过与LLM的对话加深了对书籍内容的理解。
• ravenstine：对LLM工具的使用持怀疑态度，认为大多数书籍的内容本质上是显而易见的，而LLM可能揭示出书面材料的贫乏。他还认为传统阅读方式并不是一个问题。
• geor9e：建议使用微软Edge浏览器中的Copilot侧边栏作为替代方案，以实现类似的功能。
• pillefitz：介绍了自己开发的ReadBoost工具，提供类似的书籍问答和注释功能，但提到由于动力不足而停止了进一步开发。
• l3x4ur1n：对LLM支持的电子书阅读器感兴趣，但担心安装麻烦和缺乏移动应用。
• NoLinkToMe：对工具在阅读旧书籍时的实用性表示赞赏。
• pacha3000：认为该工具没有提供明显的附加价值，特别是在已有目录的情况下。
• nathan_douglas：对该工具表示兴奋，并计划尝试使用，认为可以在讨论书籍内容时提供有价值的参考。
• slopdo：关注AI回答中可能包含剧透的问题，建议增加防止剧透的机制。
• ericol：对该工具的实现感到高兴，并表示会尝试使用。
• future10se：认为工具在多卷本书籍系列中的应用有潜力，但担心工具可能剥夺思考的过程，并建议打包成易于部署的Docker镜像。
• karolcodes：支持该项目，建议增加自动添加书籍前言的特性，以帮助读者了解必要的背景知识。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于LLM工具是否真正提供了阅读过程中的附加价值，以及是否会导致读者思考能力的下降。
• 一些用户对工具的安装复杂性和移动应用的缺乏表示关注。
• 有用户提出防止AI回答中包含剧透信息的需求。
• 总体上，用户对工具在处理复杂或结构不良的书籍内容时的潜力表示认可，但也对其在日常阅读中的必要性和可能带来的负面影响表示担忧。

BookWith – A New Reading Experience with AI
A next-generation conversational reading platform that goes beyond traditional e-book readers
📖 What is BookWith?
BookWith is an innovative e-book reader where AI becomes your reading partner. By conversing with an AI that fully understands the book's content in real time, BookWith transforms the reading experience from merely
consuming information
to
creating knowledge
.
It is more than an e-book reader: BookWith answers your questions, deepens comprehension, and offers new perspectives—your true companion for reading.
bookwith.mp4
🎯 Why BookWith?
Pain Points of Conventional E-Book Readers
❌ When you encounter something unclear you have to look it up yourself
❌ No way to check how well you understand what you've read
❌ Hard to discover relationships with content you read in the past
❌ Notes and highlights are scattered and hard to utilize
How BookWith Solves These Problems
✅ AI answers your questions on the spot
✅ Dialogue helps verify and deepen your understanding
✅ Automatically links to your past reading content
✅ Integrates annotations and AI dialogue into solid knowledge
🚀 Key Features
📚
AI Reading Assistant
An AI partner that fully understands the book's content
Context Awareness
: Grasps the content of the page you are on and answers in context
Instant Answers
: Real-time responses to questions such as "What does this term mean?" or "Summarize the author's argument."
Deep Insight Support
: Enables advanced discussions like "How can this concept be applied today?"
Full Japanese Support
: Natural Japanese dialogue with rich explanations of technical terms
Example
User: "If we apply the theory explained in this chapter to a real business scene, what happens?"
AI:   "Applying the innovation theory from Chapter 3 to actual business would…"
🎙️
AI Podcast Generation
Convert book content into conversational podcasts
podcast1.1.mp4
Automatic Script Generation
: Extract key points and convert them into a host-guest dialogue format
Optimized for 5-10 minute listenable length
Explains complex topics in an easy-to-understand conversational style
High-Quality Audio Synthesis
: Utilize Google Cloud Text-to-Speech's multi-speaker functionality
Achieves natural conversation rhythm and intonation
Supports both Japanese and English
Supports multiple languages
Seamless Experience
:
Upload a book and automatically generate a podcast
Generated audio is immediately playable
Learn key points while commuting or during movement
Use Cases
When you want to understand the summary of a long novel
Check the key points of a business book while commuting
Preview the main ideas of a technical book with audio
🧠
Multi-Layer Memory System
Innovative memory management that ensures continuity in your reading
Short-Term Memory (latest 5 entries)
Maintains the current conversation flow
Keeps context even when you turn pages
Mid-Term Memory (summary every 20 entries)
Condenses key discussion points
Sustains understanding across chapters
Long-Term Memory (vector search)
Automatically retrieves relevant information from all past dialogues
Links with learning from other books
User Profile
Learns your interests and preferences
Provides a personalized reading experience
Example
: Content from an economics book you read a week ago is automatically linked to the marketing book you are reading now.
🎨
Smart Annotation
Advanced highlighting that visualizes your thinking
Color Highlights (5 colors)
🔴 Red: Critical points
🟡 Yellow: Important concepts
🟢 Green: Ideas to practice
🔵 Blue: Questions / To-verify
Intelligent Notes

• karolcodes：支持该项目，建议增加自动添加书籍前言的特性，以帮助读者了解必要的背景知识。

• 争议焦点在于LLM工具是否真正提供了阅读过程中的附加价值，以及是否会导致读者思考能力的下降。

data.author: cadertots

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：硅谷与军事工业的结合及其历史和现实影响

不同观点：
• advisedwang：认为这是权力集团结盟的表现，类似于艾森豪威尔警告的军事工业复合体，并提到法西斯主义也曾表现为企业和国家的结合，但认为这种定义对法西斯主义的解释力有限。
• cpursley：暗示这是硅谷回归其最初的起源，即与军事相关的技术和研发。
• ecshafer：支持这种结合，认为传统国防承包商缺乏能力，需要软件公司带来新技术，如软件、机器学习和人工智能，并以Palantir、SpaceX等公司为例，说明它们在预算内、提前完成项目的能力。
• ahmeneeroe-v2：指出《纽约时报》谈论硅谷时视其为商业竞争对手和生存威胁。
• Beijinger：认为这是旧现象，引用了关于消费者技术终结的文章。
• drdrek：认为军事和民用技术之间的分离是虚假的，技术上的互相促进是不可避免的。
• vjvjvjvjghv：提到企业与政府合并的趋势，指出这种趋势的利润动机，并暗示这种现象有特定名称。
• horns4lyfe：质疑最初用于开发新技术的资金来源。
• zombot：质疑这是否是硅谷对军事的腐蚀，认为硅谷已经腐蚀了其他领域，军事也不例外。
• OrvalWintermute：讨论东西方政治体制和经济模式的差异，认为尽管西方存在问题，但相比东方仍有优势，强调了地缘政治竞争对技术中心的影响。
• electricwater：回顾硅谷的历史，认为其最初就是作为军事研发集群诞生，消费互联网阶段反而是历史上的异常，当前的再军事化是回归本源。
• asciii：建议标题应为“硅谷的再军事化”，因为硅谷最初就是由军事资源资助的。
• robg：同样提到硅谷的诞生与军事资源有关。
• johndhi：认为这种趋势可能与华尔街和MBA文化对硅谷的影响有关，指出武器制造是良好的商业机会。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到硅谷的历史与军事研发的渊源，以及当前技术和地缘政治竞争对其发展的影响。
• 争议焦点在于硅谷与军事工业结合的利弊，一些人认为这是必要的技术进步途径，另一些人则担忧这种结合对社会和政治的潜在负面影响。
• 东西方政治和经济模式的比较也是一个重要讨论点，尤其是在涉及技术发展和企业生存时。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Bluefin Linux及相关Linux项目的讨论和评价

不同观点：
• **支持和推荐Bluefin Linux**：andrewmutz强烈推荐Bluefin Linux，认为它是一个非常棒的面向开发者的Linux发行版，并提供了项目链接。
• **赞赏视频讲解**：JSR_FDED赞赏评论中提到的视频和旁白，认为比提供过少上下文的动画gif更好。
• **实际使用体验积极**：samgranieri分享了自己在mini pc上使用Bluefin Linux的体验，认为其资源消耗低，并考虑将其作为日常驱动系统替代macOS。
• **简化配置过程**：richardlblair提到使用Bluefin Linux的配置过程简单，从无到有用起来毫不费力，并可以根据需要进行调整。
• **旧硬件上的表现**：ezekg计划在一台2015年的MacBook Pro上安装Omarchy，并期待其在旧硬件上的良好表现。

补充讨论：
• **对新手不够友好**：Shank提到Bluefin Linux默认浏览器为Chromium而非Firefox，且手册中未明确说明，此外认为Hyprland和neovim对新手来说可能较难上手。
• **与其他发行版比较**：islanderfun将Bluefin Linux与crunchbang比较，认为它是一个小巧而有个性的发行版。
• **对Hyprland的兴趣**：ChocolateGod表示对Hyprland有兴趣，认为它是目前受到很多关注的 compositor/环境。
• **对配置方式的建议**：fouc分享了过去使用Linux的经历，认为Omakub和Omarchy简化了配置过程，但建议使用更声明性的配置方式如nix，而非bash脚本。
• **对项目性质的疑问**：indigodaddy提出疑问，认为此项目是否应被称为“发行版”值得商榷。
• **总体积极评价**：aus10d和k310对项目表示赞赏和支持。

争议焦点：
• **新手友好性**：Shank认为Bluefin Linux对新手不够友好，尤其是默认软件和配置工具的选择上。
• **配置方式**：fouc虽然赞赏项目简化了配置，但认为使用bash脚本不够声明性，建议采用如nix等更现代的配置方式。

总体而言，评论者们对Bluefin Linux及其相关项目多持积极态度，但也有人对其新手友好性和配置方式提出改进建议。

data.title: Speedhunters was a car culture juggernaut
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary:
Speedhunters，这个曾影响了一代车迷的汽车摄影网站，在今年四月悄然停更。该网站由Rod Chong于2008年创立，得到了电子游戏公司EA的支持，旨在连接游戏与真实汽车文化，尤其为其《极品飞车》（Need for Speed）系列提供内容参考。网站内容深入参与了《极品飞车》的制作，贡献者参与大型汽车活动并反馈给游戏开发团队。然而，Speedhunters的员工与游戏团队相对独立，外界对其与EA的关系知之甚少。

尽管Speedhunters成长为全球汽车文化的重要平台，吸引了如Larry Chen和Dino Dalle Carbonare等知名摄影师，但其命运始终与《极品飞车》绑定。许多读者直到最近才知道其与EA的关系。随着时间推移，网站逐渐失去活力，最终在没有公告的情况下停更。

不同观点：

• fat_santa表达了对Speedhunters和Hoonigan巅峰时期的喜爱，认为两者都充满了“酷”的气息。他对Ken Block的去世和这两个品牌的崩溃感到惋惜，认为当前是汽车文化的黑暗时代。不过，他仍抱有希望，相信汽车文化会再度兴盛。

Speedhunters, as we know it,
is done for
. The car photography site that shaped a generation’s automotive imagination went out with a whimper, not a bang, when publishing quietly froze in April. After I reported the news last week, past contributors flooded my inbox with notes as they sought to share their side of the story. Now that I’ve sat down with them for hours, talking over the phone and email while reaching out to other key figures in the Speedhunters saga, I’m publishing all my findings here.
One thing I want to make clear straight away is that this isn’t the comprehensive follow-up I hoped to write. Several high-ranking staffers failed to respond to my request for comment, and Electronic Arts—Speedhunters’ parent company—didn’t have anything to say, either. Still, I gained a ton of insight from five contributors who were willing to speak with me, four of whom asked to remain anonymous, citing professional and legal concerns. What’s important is they worked at the site during its heyday and managed to stick around until the bitter, uneventful end.
The story is tragic, but it can be summed up in one line: Speedhunters was never supposed to be so big in the first place.
Why Speedhunters Was Founded
Here’s an incredibly early version of the Speedhunters site, archived on the Wayback Machine with a date of May 17, 2008.
Internet Archive
Speedhunters was founded by Rod Chong in 2008 with backing from EA, the video game company that still owns the site now. It was created to connect EA with automotive culture, helping inform the content choices for its
Need for Speed
titles. In short, Speedhunters tied the games to the real world while building credibility among actual car people.
The site’s involvement with
NFS
was far deeper than most outsiders realized, as several contributors told me. They would attend massive events—think SEMA and Tokyo Auto Salon, but also the Nürburgring 24 Hours—then report back to the game’s creators. One former Speedhunters contributor told me the access they had was “unreal,” so much so that getting press credentials for virtually any car event in the world was a given.
Boots-on-the-ground content capture then made its way into games like
NFS: Shift
, with
early Speedhunters blogs featuring screengrabs and clips
from the motorsport-focused title. This continued for more than a decade, across multiple
NFS
entries.
Peep the Speedhunters windshield decal on this drifting Subaru BRZ from 2015’s
Need for Speed
reboot.
Electronic Arts
One former contributor explained to me, “I joined the creative directors in the making of one of the [NFS] games. We went to Miami and I set up a list of eight shoots that they joined me on, and so they just followed there.” They said the game’s creative director was on location, looking for insight on world-building, along with several other
Need for Speed
crew members. “There were cool moments like with that team and stuff, but they were completely, completely removed from Speedhunters. They didn’t even really know what Speedhunters was. And I think that was kind of the problem,” he explained.
Indeed, it seemed like most people outside of Speedhunters were clueless about their association with
NFS
, or at least didn’t want to speak on it. One EA game developer told
The Drive
, “Even when I worked on
NFS
, they didn’t like to talk about the relationship between EA and Speedhunters. It was [expletive] odd to say the least.”
Most of the site’s audience was totally out of the loop, too. Comment sections and Reddit threads filled with people learning Speedhunters is owned by EA just last week prove it. On one hand, this proves that Speedhunters was something special, given that its corporate tie-in was so obscured; on the other, it meant that its future was always tethered to
Need for Speed.
It Evolved Into a Global Car Culture Juggernaut
To the rest of the world, Speedhunters was the go-to spot for authentic car content. The staff wasn’t filled with pandering marketing majors; instead, they were real gearheads who went everywhere you wished you could. Household names like
Larry Chen
and
Dino Dalle Carbonare
filled the pages with beautiful and, honestly, inimitable shots. A fantastic team formed around them, and for years, Speedhunters was the dream outlet for shooters everywhere.
“I submitted my first story in 2009 to Speedhunters, and was offered a 12-month contract in 2010 to contribute regularly,” explained
Paddy McGrath
, one of Speedhunters’ most prolific photographers, over email. “It was a junior role, but I was straight out of college and pretty much into my dream job.”
Of course, it was. Everybody—myself included—wanted to be a part of what was going on there. I remember pitching a story about a built Mk5 VW GTI that was local to me in hopes of being publish

data.title: Gödel's Loophole
data.author: m-hodges
data.article_summary: 奥地利-美国逻辑学家、数学家库尔特·哥德尔在1947年研究美国入籍考试时，认为美国宪法存在一个内在矛盾，即所谓的“哥德尔漏洞”。他担心这一漏洞可能允许美国从共和体制合法转变为独裁体制，特别是基于他逃离纳粹德国的经历。尽管哥德尔向朋友奥斯卡·摩根斯坦透露了这一担忧，并通过摩根斯坦告知了阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦，但这一漏洞的具体内容从未被明确揭示。后来的学者如F. E. Guerra-Pujol猜测，该漏洞可能与宪法第五条有关，即宪法修正案的通过程序可以通过自我修正变得更容易，从而可能导致宪政体制的逐步改变。尽管这一问题引发了广泛讨论，但哥德尔的确切意思至今不明。

44812159.article_content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Alleged flaw in the United States Constitution
Kurt Gödel
in 1925
Gödel's Loophole
is a supposed "inner contradiction" in the
Constitution of the United States
which Austrian-American
logician
,
mathematician
, and
analytic philosopher
Kurt Gödel
postulated in 1947. The
loophole
would permit
America's republican structure
to be legally turned into a
dictatorship
. Gödel told his friend
Oskar Morgenstern
about the existence of the flaw and Morgenstern told
Albert Einstein
about it at the time, but Morgenstern, in his recollection of the incident in 1971, never mentioned the exact problem as Gödel saw it. This has led to speculation about the precise nature of what has come to be called "Gödel's Loophole." It has been called "one of the great unsolved problems of constitutional law" by
American constitutional law
scholar John Nowak.
[
1
]
History
[
edit
]
When Gödel was studying to take his
American citizenship test
in 1947, he came across what he called an "inner contradiction" in the
U.S. Constitution
. At the time, he was at the
Institute for Advanced Study
in
Princeton, New Jersey
, where he was good friends with Albert Einstein and Oskar Morgenstern. Gödel told Morgenstern about the flaw in the constitution, which, he said, would allow the U.S. to legally become a
fascist state
. Morgenstern tried to convince Gödel that this was very unlikely, but Gödel remained very concerned about it. He was an
Austrian
by birth and, having lived through the
1933 coup d'état
and escaped from
Nazi Germany
after the
Anschluss
, had reason to be concerned about living in a fascist dictatorship. Morgenstern had secret discussions with Gödel about his concerns and told Einstein about them.
[
2
]
[
3
]
On the day of the examination some months later, Gödel was driven to the courthouse in
Trenton, New Jersey
, by Morgenstern and Einstein, who were to be his witnesses. Both had already taken the test and become naturalized U.S. citizens. At one point during the drive, Einstein, in the front seat, turned to Gödel in the back and—knowing of Gödel's concerns–asked, "Now, Gödel, are you
really
well prepared for this examination?" According to Morgenstern, Einstein's purpose in asking this was to rattle Gödel, whose reaction amused him.
[
2
]
[
3
]
At the courthouse, witnesses normally remained outside of the room during citizenship examinations, but because Einstein, a celebrity, was involved, and because the judge,
Phillip Forman
, had administered the oath of citizenship to Einstein, all three men were invited in. During the examination, Forman asked Gödel what the government of Austria was, to which he replied: "It was a republic, but the constitution was such that it finally was changed into a dictatorship." The judge commented that this could not happen in the U.S., and Gödel responded, "Oh, yes, I can prove it"; but the judge declined to pursue the matter.
[
2
]
[
3
]
[
4
]
Nature of the loophole
[
edit
]
Since the exact nature of Gödel's Loophole has never been published, what it is, precisely, is not known. In his 2012 paper "Gödel's Loophole" F. E. Guerra-Pujol speculates that the problem involves
Article V
, which describes the process by which the Constitution can be
amended
. The
loophole
is that Article V's procedures can be applied to Article V itself. It can therefore be altered in a "downward" direction, making it easier to alter the article again in the future. So even if, as is now the case, amending the Constitution is difficult to bring about, once Article V is downwardly amended, the next attempt to do so will be easier, and the one after that easier still.
[
1
]
[
2
]
Other writers have speculated that Gödel may have had other aspects of the Constitution in mind as well, including the abuse of
gerrymandering
,
prorogation of Congress
, the
Electoral College
, and the
presidential pardon
.
[
5
]
Aftermath and reception
[
edit
]
Morgenstern's notes on the incident were published only in 2019, so no accounts before that take advantage of his recollections. Morgenstern is obviously incorrect in some details, such as the year of Gödel's citizenship test, which is established as 1947, not 1946, as Morgenstern remembers it.
[
original research?
]
Many versions of the story were published before the release of Morgenstern's notes, and they vary in their details. For instance, in mathematician and science fiction author
Rudy Rucker
's telling of the story in his 2008 novel
Mathematicians in Love
, Gödel runs to Einstein with the news and Einstein calms Gödel down.
Versions of the story can also be found in
Logical Dilemmas: The Life and Work of Kurt Gödel
(1997) by
John W. Dawson
;
E: His Life, His Thought and His Influence on Our Culture
(2006), edited by Donald Goldsmith and
Marcia Bartusiak
;
Incompleteness: The Proof and Paradox of Kurt Gödel
(2006) by
Rebecca Goldstein
;
Godel: A Life Of Logic, The Mind, And Mathematics
(2009) by John L. Casti and Werner DePauli;
Unconstituti
